README.md:
# Application records

What `aeiou-trace digest` knows about the applications whose traces it reads (`DESIGN_REVIEW.md`
§3.88). A person who uses a product may not know its storage design; the digest recognizes the
product from the paths in the trace, asks "is this X, and which version?", asks only the few
options of X that change its storage workload, and fills from the record what a short trace
cannot show. Every fact a record supplies is recorded in the digest as an assertion with the
record as its provenance, weaker than the owner's own answer, and is checked against the trace
like any answer: the trace always wins.

One directory per application, named as a user would pick it from a list, lowercase and
hyphenated. Inside:

- `application.toml`: what does not change across versions. `name` (the directory's), `display`,
  `kind` (`library`, `service`, `managed`, defined in `attributes.toml`), `summary`, `home`,
  `source` (the repository), `signatures` (globs matched against each path under the trace's
  root and against its part after any `/`, so `__*_*.distcp` matches a shard at any depth; `*`
  crosses `/`; any match identifies the application), and `mechanisms`
  (the catalog mechanisms it maps to, as `category/[class/]mechanism`).
- `<version>.toml`, one per version range the facts were read for, named by the lowest version
  it covers (`2.5.toml`): `from` (the file's stem), optional `until` (exclusive), `read` (the
  date), `sources` (what was read), then `[[option]]` entries, each a question with `choices`,
  an optional `default`, its `source` and `confidence`, and `blind_spots`, a table from a choice
  to the blind spot it causes (`attributes.toml`); `[[blind_spot]]` entries that hold whatever
  the options; and `[[assert]]` entries, what the record answers for the digest: a `template`
  glob (matched against the paths of a template), either `fact` and `value` or `question` and
  `answer` in the digest's own vocabulary (facts `candidates`, `passes`, `keys`, `requests`,
  `size`, `keep`, `writers`, `values:<field>`; questions `selection`, `size`, `order`, `origin`,
  `reuse`, `skew`, `memory`, `dependency`, `label`, each with its two candidates, see
  `aeiou-trace(1)`), a `note`, the `source` and `confidence`, and an optional
  `when = { option = "...", choice = "..." }`.

The digest picks the record whose range contains the version the person names; with none, it
takes the nearest lower record and every one of its assertions becomes a suggestion the person
confirms rather than a fact it records. `builder/tests/test_applications.py` walks every record.
The directory ships in the wheel (`builder/pyproject.toml`), and `--applications DIR` points the
digest at a checkout or at extra records.
attributes.toml:
# The vocabulary of the application records (DESIGN_REVIEW.md §3.88): what `aeiou-trace digest`
# knows about the applications whose traces it reads, so that a person who uses a product and
# does not know its storage design can answer from a list. One directory per application,
# `application.toml` for what does not change across versions and `<version>.toml` per version
# range the facts were read for; `builder/aeiou/applications.py` refuses a record that uses a
# word not defined here. The three rules: the trace always wins (a record fills what a short
# trace cannot show and never overrides what it does); a record's facts are assertions weaker
# than the owner's, with their own provenance; a record never claims a version it was not read
# for. Adding a product or a version is a new file.

applications_version = 1

# kind: what runs where the trace is taken
[kind]
library = "a library in the application's own process; the trace is the application's and the library's calls are in it"
service = "a self-hosted service; the trace is of the service's processes, and the application that queries it is traced separately"
managed = "a managed (hosted) service; its storage is the vendor's and never under test here, so only what the client does on its own storage is traceable"

# confidence: how a fact in a record was read
[confidence]
high = "read in the application's source, or in its documentation for the version the record names"
medium = "read in documentation that does not name the version, in a configuration file of another version, or inferred from the application's design"

# blind_spot: I/O the application does that an strace does not show as reads and writes
[blind_spot]
mmap = "the application maps its files and reads them through page faults; the trace shows the mmap and none of the reads, so the digest undercounts"
io_uring = "the application reads through io_uring; the trace shows io_uring_enter and not the requests, so the digest undercounts"
object = "the application keeps data on an object store; the strace shows only its local cache, and the request log (PROJECT_BRIEF.md item 49) is needed for the rest"
diskann/0.7.toml:
from = "0.7"
read = "2026-10-29"
sources = [
  "workloads/vector-search/diskann-build/kit (diskannpy 0.7.0, traced 2026-10-02)",
  "workloads/vector-search/diskann-search/kit (diskannpy 0.7.0, traced 2026-10-02)",
]

[[option]]
name = "num_nodes_to_cache"
question = "Does the search cache graph nodes in memory (num_nodes_to_cache above zero), so the hottest sectors are never read?"
choices = ["no cache", "cached nodes"]
default = "no cache"
source = "https://github.com/microsoft/DiskANN (StaticDiskIndex.search's num_nodes_to_cache)"
confidence = "medium"
diskann/application.toml:
name = "diskann"
display = "DiskANN"
kind = "library"
summary = "Microsoft's disk-resident graph index (Vamana): a build writes the graph with the vectors inline in 4 KiB sectors plus the PQ tables; a search walks the graph with a beam of positioned reads"
home = "https://github.com/microsoft/DiskANN"
source = "https://github.com/microsoft/DiskANN"
signatures = ["*_disk.index", "*_pq_pivots.bin", "*_pq_compressed.bin", "*_sample_data.bin"]
mechanisms = ["vector-search/diskann-build", "vector-search/diskann-search"]
faiss/1.15.toml:
from = "1.15"
read = "2026-10-29"
sources = [
  "workloads/vector-search/faiss-ivf-ondisk/kit (faiss-cpu 1.15.1, traced 2026-10-01)",
]

[[blind_spot]]
kind = "mmap"
note = "OnDiskInvertedLists maps the lists file and never calls read on it; the probed lists reach memory through page faults the trace does not show (the mechanism's abstract declares posix mmap)"
source = "workloads/vector-search/faiss-ivf-ondisk/faiss_ivf_ondisk.py"
confidence = "high"
faiss/application.toml:
name = "faiss"
display = "FAISS"
kind = "library"
summary = "Meta's vector-search library; its on-disk inverted lists (OnDiskInvertedLists) are a file the index maps, under names the application chooses, so no path identifies it"
home = "https://github.com/facebookresearch/faiss"
source = "https://github.com/facebookresearch/faiss"
signatures = []
mechanisms = ["vector-search/faiss-ivf-ondisk"]
lmcache/0.5.toml:
from = "0.5"
read = "2026-10-29"
sources = [
  "https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/v0.5.5/lmcache/v1/storage_backend/local_disk_backend.py (_key_to_path, write_file, read_file)",
  "https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/v0.5.5/lmcache/utils.py (CacheEngineKey.to_string: model@world_size@worker_id@chunk_hash_hex@dtype, '/' in the model name written '-')",
  "workloads/kvcache/lmcache-local-disk/kit (LMCache 0.5.5 under vLLM 0.30, traced 2026-10)",
]

[[option]]
name = "use_odirect"
question = "Does the local-disk backend open its files with O_DIRECT (LMCache's use_odirect)?"
choices = ["buffered", "O_DIRECT"]
default = "buffered"
source = "https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/v0.5.5/lmcache/v1/storage_backend/local_disk_backend.py"
confidence = "high"

[[option]]
name = "local_cpu"
question = "Is a CPU memory tier in front of the disk (LMCache's local_cpu), so that a hit in it never reaches the disk?"
choices = ["no CPU tier", "CPU tier on"]
source = "https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/v0.5.5/lmcache/v1/storage_manager.py"
confidence = "high"
lmcache/application.toml:
name = "lmcache"
display = "LMCache"
kind = "library"
summary = "the KV-cache layer of vLLM: a prefix's KV chunks stored once under a hashed key and loaded on a prefix hit, to a local disk or a shared file system"
home = "https://lmcache.ai"
source = "https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache"
signatures = ["*@*@*@*@*.pt"]
mechanisms = ["kvcache/lmcache-local-disk", "kvcache/lmcache-shared-fs"]
milvus/3.0.toml:
from = "3.0"
read = "2026-10-29"
sources = [
  "https://milvus.io/docs/architecture_overview.md (v3.0.x docs: object storage persists data and index files; query nodes cache what they serve; tiered storage from 2.6.4)",
  "https://milvus.io/docs/mmap.md (v3.0.x docs: queryNode.mmap.vectorField/vectorIndex/scalarField/scalarIndex; mapped files under localStorage.path/mmap; DISKANN not mappable)",
  "https://milvus.io/docs/disk_index.md (v3.0.x docs: DISKANN index files under /var/lib/milvus/data, NVMe recommended)",
  "https://github.com/milvus-io/milvus/blob/master/configs/milvus.yaml (localStorage.path /var/lib/milvus/data/, minio.rootPath files, index.storePathVersion layouts, queryNode.mmap defaults, tieredStorage warmup and eviction)",
  "https://milvus.io/docs/release_notes.md (3.0.3 of 2026-10-14; Storage V3 'Loon' off by default; Vortex and Lance formats)",
]

[[blind_spot]]
kind = "object"
note = "segments and index files persist on the object store (minio.rootPath 'files' in the bucket); an strace of a query node shows only what it pulls to local storage and memory, never the object requests"
source = "https://milvus.io/docs/architecture_overview.md"
confidence = "high"

[[option]]
name = "index"
question = "Which index type serves the collection: an in-memory index (HNSW, IVF, AUTOINDEX) loaded whole, or DISKANN on the query node's local disk?"
choices = ["in-memory index", "DISKANN on local disk"]
default = "in-memory index"
source = "https://milvus.io/docs/disk_index.md"
confidence = "medium"

[[option]]
name = "mmap_vector_field"
question = "Is memory-mapped loading on for the raw vector data (queryNode.mmap.vectorField, or mmap.enabled on the collection)?"
choices = ["loaded into memory", "memory-mapped"]
default = "memory-mapped"
source = "https://github.com/milvus-io/milvus/blob/master/configs/milvus.yaml says vectorField: true; https://milvus.io/docs/mmap.md says the four keys default to false after 2.4.10; the configuration file is taken as the newer source"
confidence = "medium"
[option.blind_spots]
"memory-mapped" = "mmap"

[[option]]
name = "mmap_vector_index"
question = "Is memory-mapped loading on for the vector index (queryNode.mmap.vectorIndex, or mmap.enabled on the index)?"
choices = ["loaded into memory", "memory-mapped"]
default = "loaded into memory"
source = "https://github.com/milvus-io/milvus/blob/master/configs/milvus.yaml (vectorIndex: false)"
confidence = "high"
[option.blind_spots]
"memory-mapped" = "mmap"

[[option]]
name = "tiered_storage"
question = "Is tiered storage eviction on (queryNode.segcore.tieredStorage.evictionEnabled), so that evicted field data and indexes are fetched again from the object store on demand?"
choices = ["eviction off", "eviction on"]
default = "eviction off"
source = "https://github.com/milvus-io/milvus/blob/master/configs/milvus.yaml (evictionEnabled: false)"
confidence = "high"
milvus/application.toml:
name = "milvus"
display = "Milvus"
kind = "service"
summary = "a vector database service: segments of vectors, scalar fields, and indexes persisted on an object store (MinIO, S3, Azure Blob), loaded by query nodes into memory, memory-mapped files, or a local disk index (DISKANN) under its local storage path"
home = "https://milvus.io"
source = "https://github.com/milvus-io/milvus"
signatures = ["index_files/*", "index_v1/*", "insert_log/*", "delta_log/*", "stats_log/*"]
mechanisms = []
pytorch-dcp/2.14.toml:
from = "2.14"
until = "2.15"
read = "2026-10-29"
sources = [
  "https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.checkpoint.html",
  "workloads/checkpointing/dcp-save/kit/save.py and its README (torch 2.14.1 traced 2026-10)",
  "workloads/checkpointing/dcp-load/kit/load.py and its README (torch 2.14.1 traced 2026-10)",
]

[[option]]
name = "single_file_per_rank"
question = "Does each rank write one shard file per checkpoint (FileSystemWriter's single_file_per_rank), or one file per item?"
choices = ["one file per rank", "one file per item"]
default = "one file per rank"
source = "https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.checkpoint.html"
confidence = "high"

[[option]]
name = "sync_files"
question = "Does the writer fsync each shard before the checkpoint is declared complete (FileSystemWriter's sync_files)?"
choices = ["fsync on", "fsync off"]
default = "fsync on"
source = "https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.checkpoint.html"
confidence = "high"

[[assert]]
template = "__*_*.distcp"
question = "size"
answer = "per-path"
note = "a rank's shard holds the bytes of its plan's items; the bytes are a property of the file, the same at every load"
source = "workloads/checkpointing/dcp-load/kit/params.py (the plan read from .metadata)"
confidence = "high"

[[assert]]
template = "__*_*.distcp"
question = "label"
answer = "checkpoint"
note = "the shards are a training job's state, saved to survive a failure and loaded to resume"
source = "https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.checkpoint.html"
confidence = "high"
pytorch-dcp/application.toml:
name = "pytorch-dcp"
display = "PyTorch Distributed Checkpoint"
kind = "library"
summary = "torch.distributed.checkpoint: every rank writes its shard of the model and optimizer state per checkpoint; rank 0 writes the plan as .metadata; a load reads each rank's items from the shards"
home = "https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.checkpoint.html"
source = "https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/tree/main/torch/distributed/checkpoint"
signatures = ["__*_*.distcp", ".metadata"]
mechanisms = ["checkpointing/dcp-save", "checkpointing/dcp-load"]
qdrant/1.19.toml:
from = "1.19"
read = "2026-10-29"
sources = [
  "https://qdrant.tech/documentation/concepts/storage/ (segments; vectors always in a memory-mapped file, memory tier cached or cold; payload in Gridstore, cached or cold; the WAL)",
  "https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/releases (1.19.0 of 2026-08-05: single-file mmap vector storage on by default for immutable segments, payload storage through io_uring; 1.20.0 of 2026-10-22: hnsw_config.inline_storage, madvise(WILLNEED) prefetch on on-disk search; RocksDB removed in 1.18)",
]

[[blind_spot]]
kind = "mmap"
note = "vectors are always kept in a memory-mapped file and scored through the mapping; the trace shows the mmap and madvise calls and none of the reads"
source = "https://qdrant.tech/documentation/concepts/storage/"
confidence = "high"

[[blind_spot]]
kind = "io_uring"
note = "payload storage reads go through io_uring since 1.19; the trace shows io_uring_enter, not the requests"
source = "https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/releases (1.19.0)"
confidence = "medium"

[[option]]
name = "vectors_memory"
question = "Which memory tier holds the vectors: cached (the file preloaded into the page cache at start) or cold (paged in on access)?"
choices = ["cached", "cold"]
default = "cached"
source = "https://qdrant.tech/documentation/concepts/storage/ (vectors.memory; memmap_threshold sets the default)"
confidence = "high"

[[option]]
name = "payload_memory"
question = "Which memory tier holds the payload: cached or cold?"
choices = ["cached", "cold"]
default = "cold"
source = "https://qdrant.tech/documentation/concepts/storage/ (payload.memory)"
confidence = "high"

[[option]]
name = "hnsw_memory"
question = "Which memory tier holds the HNSW graph: cached or cold?"
choices = ["cached", "cold"]
source = "https://qdrant.tech/documentation/concepts/storage/ (hnsw_config.memory)"
confidence = "medium"
qdrant/application.toml:
name = "qdrant"
display = "Qdrant"
kind = "service"
summary = "a vector database service: collections in segments, each with its vector storage (always a memory-mapped file), its payload storage (Gridstore), and its HNSW index, written through a write-ahead log"
home = "https://qdrant.tech"
source = "https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant"
signatures = ["collections/*/segments/*/vector_storage/*", "collections/*/segments/*/payload_storage/*", "collections/*/wal/*"]
mechanisms = []
safetensors/0.8.toml:
from = "0.8"
read = "2026-10-29"

  "workloads/model-loading/safetensors-load/kit (safetensors 0.8.0 under transformers 5.18, traced 2026-10-01)",

[[blind_spot]]

display = "safetensors"

source = "https://github.com/huggingface/safetensors"
